summary: The document describes a Hospital Patient Portal that claims to use HIPAA‑compliant AES‑256 encryption at rest and enforces access control via OAuth2 RBAC roles. No further architectural details, data flow, compliance mappings, or operational specifications are provided.

risk_factors.title: Missing Audit Trail and Log Immutability
risk_factors.description: The document does not specify any mechanism for immutable audit logging of PHI access, which is required by HIPAA and GDPR for accountability.
risk_factors.mitigation: Implement tamper‑evident audit logs (e.g., append‑only storage with digital signatures) and define retention policies.

risk_factors.title: Undefined Encryption Key Management
risk_factors.description: While AES‑256 encryption at rest is mentioned, there is no description of key generation, rotation, storage, or access controls.
risk_factors.mitigation: Adopt a hardware security module (HSM) or cloud KMS, define key lifecycle procedures, and enforce least‑privilege access to keys.

verification.claim: Risk: Undefined Encryption Key Management — While AES‑256 encryption at rest is mentioned, there is no description of key generation, rotation, storage, or access controls.

risk_factors.title: Absent RTO/RPO Targets

risk_factors.mitigation: Define backup frequency, replication strategy, and automated failover processes that meet the stated RTO/RPO benchmarks.
